objective: Explain the schemes-knob adjoint finding mechanistically from discretization and stability theory, and convert the explanation into admissibility thresholds in the physics rules so scheme choices are justified by stability and differentiability arguments rather than by folklore
rationale: The lab has an unusually clean experimental table and no mechanism for it. On one mesh and one cut, four momentum-advection choices give adjoint errors of 8.95 percent, then 0.849, then 0.157, then 0.041, against Krylov counts of 719, 41, 223 and 41 respectively. The pair that matters is the first two: one word changes, same formal order, same gradient-correction term, only the minimum and maximum stencil selection removed, and the error drops by a factor of 10.5 while the Krylov count drops by 17.5. At operator level the same lever collapses the cross-residual from 329 times the right-hand side to 1.35e-02 times it, a collapse of four orders, while the boundary-condition lever moves the error without touching the operator, which is how the record already words it: one lever hides the defect and the other repairs the operator. A third result rules out the easy story that this is a parallel artefact, because the same limiter combination breaks the serial adjoint on a different case at 92.8 percent while its one-word control lands at 0.121 percent. The doctrine that fell out is already recorded, that decomposition invariance certifies consistency and not correctness. What is missing is why, and the shape of the answer is available from theory rather than from more runs: a limiter is a non-differentiable, state-dependent stencil selection, so the discrete residual it defines is only piecewise differentiable, and a reverse-mode tape differentiates the branch that was taken rather than the operator the residual defines. The primal side has an independent witness that the same class of instability is not exotic: the TMR airfoil family fails to reach steady state on 8 of 9 rungs under second-order momentum advection, oscillates antisymmetrically on a symmetric case, and settles only to a residual cycle of about 3e-4 under a total-variation-diminishing scheme that never flattens over 15,000 iterations. Both sides are stability and differentiability questions, and neither has ever been treated as one. Axis A: reading-kind at zero solver cost. Axis B: 0. Axis C: 0.

cost_basis: measured; every arm this explains has already been paid for and its logs are retained, the stability analysis is done by hand, and the deliverable is a derivation plus threshold values, so no solver time is spent and no case is opened
expected_knowledge_gain: Three distinguishable outcomes. One: the non-differentiable-stencil account predicts the observed ordering across all four schemes and the serial reproduction, in which case the lab has a rule that says in advance which schemes are admissible when a discrete adjoint is wanted, and that rule becomes numbers in the physics rules rather than a habit. Two: the account predicts the ordering but not the Krylov counts, which separates the accuracy defect from the conditioning defect and says they are two mechanisms rather than one. Three: the analysis contradicts the table, which would mean the experimental attribution is wrong and the whole chain from the schemes lever to the operator-level collapse needs re-reading before anything is written up. The primal-side airfoil oscillation gets the same treatment and either falls into the same family or is separated from it with a reason.
sequencing: Ride-along under strategy rule 4: depth on problems already open, no new compute.
gate: STRATEGY PROOF CLAUSE, verbatim: 'Discretization & stability theory: LeVeque FV book + von Neumann analysis toolkit -> PROOF: scheme choices in physics_rules justified by stability regions, not folklore; the schemes-knob DAFoam finding explained mechanistically.' Operationalised in two halves, both required. Half one: a written mechanism for the four-scheme table that predicts, from analysis rather than from the table, the sign and approximate size of the ordering across the four choices and the serial reproduction at 92.8 percent, stated before it is checked against the recorded numbers. Half two: the admissibility statement lands as numbers in the physics rules, naming which momentum-advection and gradient choices are admissible when a discrete adjoint is the product and what the stability argument for each threshold is, with no constant left in workflow code. An explanation that only fits the table after seeing it, or that lands as prose with no threshold, fails.
